items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I spent an association with him for 17 years.

ctx.x: Because you can fit a lot of music on CDs as opposed to — records used to get about twenty minutes. You have also recorded with a whole number of people, including Leon Redbone. What was that like?
Well the first time met Leon Redbone was in Eddie Condon’s, I was playing there and he was looking for a clarinet player. And he sent in a fellow named Tom Waits, who © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

probably you are familiar with. So he was at the bar and I was playing the clarinet and I knew he was coming in, I knew somebody was coming in to hear me play so I said, “Mr. Waits, how do you do?” And he said, “I’m with Leon Redbone’s entourage.” So he had a couple of guys there. Leon wasn’t there. And Leon said that he did hire me. We were supposed to go to Cleveland and I got a good word from Tom Waits, and everybody else was there. So the next day I left for Cleveland, Ohio, and I went in the backstage…
